facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Ctenosauriscus was discovered in early 1871 near Göttingen, Germany.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in early 1871 in the Bremke dell locality, near the county of Göttingen.

facts.statement: The species was first described in 1902 by Friedrich von Huene, who initially named it Ctenosaurus koeneni.
facts.quote: It remained undescribed until 1902, when German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene designated it to the new species Ctenosaurus koeneni.

facts.statement: The genus name was changed to Ctenosauriscus in 1964 by Oskar Kuhn because the original name was already taken by a lizard.
facts.quote: The name Ctenosaurus was preoccupied by a species of iguanid lizard (now called Ctenosaura), so a new generic name, Ctenosauriscus, was erected by paleontologist Oskar Kuhn in 1964.

facts.statement: A major redescription of the holotype was published in 2011 by a team of six paleontologists.
facts.quote: A redescription of the holotype was published by Richard J. Butler, Stephen L. Brusatte, Mike Reich, Sterling J. Nesbitt, Rainer R. Schoch and Jahn J. Hornung in 2011.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus lived during the latest Olenekian stage of the Early Triassic, approximately 247.5 to 247.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in latest Olenekian deposits around 247.5-247.2 million years old, making it one of the first known archosaurs.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is an extinct sail-backed archosaur found in Early Triassic deposits in Lower Saxony, northern Germany.
facts.quote: Ctenosauriscus (meaning "Ctenosaura-like") is an extinct genus of sail-backed poposauroid archosaur from Early Triassic deposits of Lower Saxony in northern Germany.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is distinguished by a prominent sail-like back formed from elongated neural spines on its vertebrae.
facts.quote: The most prominent feature of Ctenosauriscus is its sail-like back, formed from elongated neural spines of the dorsal and cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is most similar to the ctenosauriscid Arizonasaurus, which lived in the Middle Triassic of the southwestern United States.
facts.quote: Among ctenosauriscids, Ctenosauriscus is most similar to Arizonasaurus from the Middle Triassic of the southwestern United States.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Ctenosauriscus can reach up to 12 times the height of the vertebral bodies.
facts.quote: Both of these ctenosauriscids have elongated vertebrae spines up to 12 times the height of the bodies of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 1998 study hypothesized that Ctenosauriscus was bipedal and that its sail helped absorb forces from walking on two legs.
facts.quote: A 1998 study proposed that Ctenosauriscus was bipedal and that its elongated neural spines served to absorb the forces exerted from walking on two legs.

facts.statement: A 2011 study rejected the bipedal hypothesis, arguing that the spine's mechanics would require impossible muscle connections to the knee.
facts.quote: In the 2011 redescription of Ctenosauriscus, the authors rejected this idea because for forces on the spine to meet at the knee joint, muscles would have to form a direct connection between the knee and the back.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the sail's weight distribution would have made bipedal locomotion difficult or impossible for Ctenosauriscus.
facts.quote: The sail of Ctenosauriscus would also have shifted its center of weight toward the front of the body, making bipedal locomotion difficult or impossible.

facts.statement: Xiphosurans (horseshoe crabs) found in the same formation may have been prey for Ctenosauriscus.
facts.quote: Xiphosurans are also known from the formation, and may have been a source of prey for the archosaurs, which were dispersing across northern pangea at the time.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus lived in the Early Triassic Solling Formation of Northern Germany.
facts.quote: Ctenosauriscus lived in the Early Triassic Solling Formation of Northern Germany.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus inhabited an arid floodplain environment with dry sabkha-like areas and wetter zones resembling modern swamps.
facts.quote: Its environment was an arid Floodplain, with dry, Sabkha-like environments and wetter areas comparable to modern swamps and other stagnant lakes.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is considered one of the oldest known archosaurs, alongside Vytshegdosuchus and Xilousuchus.
facts.quote: Ctenosauriscus is one of the oldest archosaurs to date, along with Vytshegdosuchus from Russia and probably Xilousuchus, a ctenosauriscid from China.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in early 1871 at the locality of Bremke dell near the Göttingen county.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue descubierto a principios de 1871 en la localidad de Bremke dell, cerca del condado de Göttingen.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus was found in the Solling Formation, which was deposited approximately 247.5 to 247.2 million years ago during the last stage of the Olenekian.
facts.quote: Ctenosauriscus se encontró en la Formación Solling, que se depositó hace unos 247,5 a 247,2 millones de años en la última etapa del Olenekiense.

facts.statement: Paleontologist B. Krebs redescribed the holotype and reclassified Ctenosauriscus as an archosaur based on similarities with the pseudosuchian Hypselorhachis from the Middle Triassic Manda Beds of Tanzania.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo B. Krebs redescribió el holotipo y reclasificó a Ctenosauriscus como un arcosaurio basándose en las similitudes con el pseudosuquio Hypselorhachis de los lechos de Manda del Triásico Medio de Tanzania.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature of Ctenosauriscus is its sail-shaped back, formed by elongated neural spines from the dorsal and cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: La característica más destacada de Ctenosauriscus es su dorso en forma de vela, formada por espinas neurales alargadas de las vértebras dorsales y cervicales.

facts.statement: Among ctenosauriscids, Ctenosauriscus is most similar to Arizonasaurus from the Middle Triassic of the southwestern United States; both have elongated vertebral spines up to 12 times the height of the vertebral bodies.
facts.quote: Entre los ctenosauriscidos, Ctenosauriscus es más similar a Arizonasaurus del Triásico medio del suroeste de los Estados Unidos. Ambos ctenosauriscidos tienen espinas vertebrales alargadas de hasta 12 veces la altura de los cuerpos de las vértebras.

facts.statement: A 1998 study proposed that Ctenosauriscus was bipedal and that its elongated neural spines served to absorb forces exerted while walking on two legs.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 1998 propuso que Ctenosauriscus era bípedo y que sus espinas neurales alargadas servían para absorber las fuerzas ejercidas al caminar sobre dos piernas.

facts.statement: In the 2011 redescription, authors rejected the bipedal hypothesis because for forces on the spine to meet at the knee joint, muscles would have to form a direct connection between the knee and the back.
facts.quote: En la redescripción de Ctenosauriscus de 2011, los autores rechazaron esta idea porque para que las fuerzas sobre la columna se encontraran en la articulación de la rodilla, los músculos tendrían que formar una conexión directa entre la rodilla y la espalda.

facts.statement: The sail of Ctenosauriscus would have shifted its center of weight toward the front of the body, making or preventing bipedal locomotion.
facts.quote: La vela de Ctenosauriscus también habría desplazado su centro de peso hacia la parte delantera del cuerpo, dificultando o imposibilitando la locomoción bípeda.

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is one of the oldest known archosaurs to date, alongside Vytshegdosuchus from Russia and likely Xilousuchus, a ctenosauriscid from China.
facts.quote: Ctenosauriscus es uno de los arcosaurios más antiguos hasta la fecha, junto con Vytshegdosuchus de Rusia y probablemente Xilousuchus, un ctenosauriscido de China.

facts.statement: The parent group of Ctenosauriscus is Ctenosauriscidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ctenosauriscidae

facts.statement: Ctenosauriscus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
